claim: Two independent methods put the experimental reference's own heterogeneity sigma at 2.83-2.84 kcal/mol (A: matched |dQ|<=0.1 pairs, sigma 2.8437 from 1002 pairs; B: moment decomposition [V(E-Q)+V(E-L)-V(Q-L)]/2 = 2.8330), implying an oracle MAE of about 2.26 kcal/mol.
value_found: A sigma_ref=2.843664 (n_pairs=1002, sd(dE)=4.021548, row-orientation triu, ddof=1); A under the alternative ascending-Q orientation = 2.850849 (identical pair set, different sign convention of the mean); A 2nd-moment variant = 2.853856. B sigma_ref=2.833038 (V(E-Q)=9.070821, V(E-L)=12.019068, V(Q-L)=5.037678). A-B=0.010626. Oracle MAE: Gaussian-form 2.268916 (from A) and 2.260437 (from B); empirical heavy-tailed form from the same 1002 pairs = mean|dE|/sqrt(2) = 1.9617. CLAIM 11: correct pooled within-molecule SD = 9.965372 (86 molecules, 210 rows); the naive var-squared formula gives 165.262271 (mean(var^2) unweighted = 173.7653, rms = 173.7653); fragment-pair grouping: correct 1.537043, naive 3.842202.
unit: bond observation (543 benchmark rows); methods A and B use observation pairs drawn from those rows (1002 pairs span 468 distinct observations in 372 distinct molecules), not independent measurement replicates
method: Own script /tmp/verify5/verify.py (+ /tmp/verify5/checks2.py, dupdiag.py, clusci.py), reading data/normalized_views/experimental_benchmark.tsv directly with pandas and cross-checking against data/source_data/experimental_source_tables.xlsx via openpyxl; ran `python /tmp/verify5/verify.py`. No import of the original workstream modules. Methods A/B implemented from the formula as written in the claim, plus two independent A orientations (triu and ascending-Q searchsorted), ddof 0/1, float vs decimal-exact tolerance, row bootstrap and molecule-cluster bootstrap.
notes: Both arithmetic values reproduce to the digit from the raw TSV, and the xlsx workbook agrees with the TSV to 0.0 max abs difference on E, Q, L and R, so the inputs are not in dispute. A and B agree to 0.011 kcal/mol, but they are NOT independent: B is an algebraic identity for any three vectors (predicted sd(Q-L)=2.2444772572 equals observed exactly, residual 4.4e-16), and cov(E-Q,E-L) = 8.026105 = sigma_ref_sq, which is the same quantity the formula is solving for, so the 'self-consistency' check is a tautology, not evidence. Method B's own assumption (reference error uncorrelated with the channel errors) is violated directionally: the quantum channel is demonstrably derived from the DB that the experiment correlates with, so B is an upper bound. Method A is also biased upward because |dQ|<=0.1 pairs are chemically near-identical but not identical (residual true-BDE variation is included). Caveats on the sigma: (a) the tolerance is a hard boundary - a stricter decimal-exact |dQ|<=0.1 admits 29 more pairs and gives 2.823349; a looser 0.2 gives 2.749390, 0.5 gives 2.732079, 1.0 gives 2.816939, 2.0 gives 2.916661 - so 2.84 is a local high point of a U-shaped scan, not a stable plateau (the claim's 2.83-2.84 agreement is between two formulas whose difference is 0.0106, far smaller than the 0.1-0.2 spread across the tolerance scan); (b) 1002 pairs are not 1002 independent draws (468 rows, 372 molecules, 4.3 pairs per involved row), and the 543 experimental values contain only 284 distinct numbers with the top value reused 9 times, so the effective n behind the CI is much smaller than nominal; the deduplicated molecule-cluster bootstrap widens the CI to A [2.354, 3.233] and B [2.515, 3.094] (point means 2.835 and 2.827). A naive row bootstrap instead produces a downward-biased CI for A (2.03-3.09) and mean 2.51 because resampled duplicate rows inject exact (0,0) pairs - a resampling artifact, not instability of the estimator. The oracle MAE of 2.26 is the Gaussian-form number and is arithmetically correct (2.2604-2.2689) but the matched-pair distribution is strongly heavy-tailed (skew 0.807, excess kurtosis 3.19; median |dE| 1.90 vs mean 2.77), so the empirical oracle MAE from the same pairs is 1.96, i.e. about 13 percent below 2.26; the ~2.26 figure is thus the high end of the floor range and is contradicted by its own matched-pair empirical shape. Claim 11's ~165 is exactly reproducible as the nested-squared-variance bug sqrt(average(var^2, weights=n-1)) applied to single-observation groups; the correct pooled within-molecule SD is 9.965, and the correct value for the 4 repeated fragment pairs is 1.537 (the ~165 bug also corrupts the fragment-pair number to 3.84).
